definition_zh: 导航；航行；确定位置并找到路线的过程，也指网页或系统的导览结构
definition_en: the process of finding a position and a route, the act of sailing, or the menu structure that guides users through a site
core_image: 船在无岸的海上凭星位与海图校正方向，一步步靠近港口
scene: 浓雾里看不见岸，船长靠罗盘方位和灯塔的间隔校正航向，慢慢贴近港口。With no shore in sight, the captain corrects the course by compass bearing and the spacing of lighthouses, a patient art of navigation.
sceneCN: 这里 navigation 指「确定位置并找到航线的过程」（第 2 个义项：靠方位与地标不断校正）；句意为浓雾中看不见岸，船长凭罗盘与灯塔间距修正航向，慢慢驶近港口。图中可辨识物件：罗盘、海图、灯塔、雾中的船首；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 航行；导航；导览结构（不可数）

senses.title: Sailing on water
senses.definition: the act of sailing or steering a vessel along a route
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶船只沿航线行驶的行为
senses.example: Navigation on the river began before roads were built.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路还没有修好之前，河上航行就已开始。
senses.why: navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive' is literally ship-driving, so the oldest sense is the movement of a hull through water.
senses.whyCN: navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」，字面就是「驾船」；最古老的含义正是船体在水上的移动。

senses.title: Position fixing and route finding
senses.definition: the process of determining where one is and which course leads to the destination
senses.definitionCN: 确定自己在哪里、哪条航线通向目的地的过程
senses.example: The captain corrected the course by compass and lighthouses.
senses.exampleCN: 船长凭罗盘与灯塔校正了航向。
senses.why: the core of navigation is two questions, where am I and where next; every instrument serves one of them.
senses.whyCN: 导航的核心是两个问题：我在哪里、下一步往哪；每件仪器都在为其中之一服务。

senses.title: Website navigation
senses.definition: the menus, links and layout that let a user move through a site or app
senses.definitionCN: 让用户在网站或应用中移动的菜单、链接与布局
senses.example: Clear navigation kept visitors from leaving the site.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的导航让访客没有离开网站。
senses.why: a user is also a traveller: the menu is a chart of the site, and a bad chart produces the digital equivalent of being lost.
senses.whyCN: 用户也是行者：菜单是网站的海图，海图糟糕就会产生数字版的迷路。

senses.title: Animal navigation
senses.definition: the ability of animals to orient and travel toward a goal over long distances
senses.definitionCN: 动物辨向并长距离前往目标的能力
senses.example: Monarch butterflies manage navigation across a continent.
senses.exampleCN: 帝王蝶能完成跨大陆的导航。
senses.why: biology uses the word because the same two questions apply without instruments: where am I, and which way is home.
senses.whyCN: 生物学使用这个词，因为同样两个问题在没有仪器时也成立：我在哪，家在哪边。

senses.title: Air and space navigation
senses.definition: plotting and correcting a course through the air or in orbit
senses.definitionCN: 在空中或轨道上规划并修正航线
senses.example: Space navigation relies on signals from ground stations.
senses.exampleCN: 航天导航依赖地面站信号。
senses.why: as the medium changes, the instruments change, but the loop of fix, compare and correct remains.
senses.whyCN: 介质改变，仪器随之改变，但「定位、比对、修正」的循环不变。

senses.title: Navigation technology
senses.definition: the instruments and systems that support positioning and routing
senses.definitionCN: 支持定位与选路的仪器与系统
senses.example: The app's navigation depends on four satellites.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的导航依赖四颗卫星。
senses.why: metonymy lets the activity name its tools, so navigation can mean the equipment that makes it possible.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让活动命名其工具，因此 navigation 也可以指使活动得以进行的设备。

senses.title: Inland waterway transport
senses.definition: the movement of goods or people on rivers and canals
senses.definitionCN: 在河流与运河上运送货物或人员
senses.example: Inland navigation carries coal along the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 内河航运沿运河运送煤炭。
senses.why: the commercial sense narrows the old sailing sense to a transport mode counted in tonnage.
senses.whyCN: 商业义把古老的航行义收窄为一种以吨位计量的运输方式。

senses.title: The science or skill of navigating
senses.definition: the body of knowledge and technique required to find and follow a route
senses.definitionCN: 寻找并沿路线行进所需的知识与技术总体
senses.example: Navigation was taught as a mathematical art.
senses.exampleCN: 导航曾被当作一门数学技艺来教授。
senses.why: a practice that can be taught becomes a discipline, and the noun shifts from doing to knowing how.
senses.whyCN: 可以教授的实践会成为一门学问，名词便从「做」转向「知道怎么做」。

intro.en: Navigation comes from Latin navigatio, from navigare 'to sail', itself navis 'ship' plus agere 'to drive'. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: navigation 来自拉丁 navigatio，源自动词 navigare「航行」，而 navigare 由 navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」构成。它在 16 世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Navis meant 'ship, boat'; it belongs to an old Indo-European word for a vessel and survives in navy and in naval.
items.cn: navis 意为「船、舟」；它属于古老的印欧语「船」词，留在 navy 与 naval 中。

items.en: Agere meant 'to drive, lead, do'; it is the verb behind agent, act and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为「驾驶、引领、做」；它是 agent、act 与 agenda 背后的动词。

items.en: Navis plus agere produced navigare, 'to sail, steer a ship'; the compound is literal, not metaphorical.
items.cn: navis 加 agere 构成 navigare「航行、驾船」；这个复合是字面的，不是比喻。

items.en: The noun navigatio 'a sailing, a voyage' supplied the English word through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 navigatio「航行、航程」在 16 世纪经法语提供英语词形。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word extended to animal orientation and to the menus that guide users through software, both treating travel as a path toward a goal.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到动物辨向，以及引导用户使用软件的菜单；两者都把行进当作通往目标的路径。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation is not exactly fixed, and the pre-Indo-European origin of navis is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；navis 在印欧语之前的来源属于重构，而非直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same navis plus agere family; group two holds related travel and guidance concepts.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 navis 加 agere 词族的形式；第二组是相关的行进与引导概念。

entries.definition: Relating to navigation; it must modify a noun such as aid or system, while navigation names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 与导航有关的；必须修饰 aid 或 system 之类名词，而 navigation 命名活动。

entries.definition: Describing water or an aircraft that can be navigated; it judges the route, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 描述可通航的水域或可驾驶的航空器；评判路线，而非动作。

entries.definition: A person who navigates; the -or suffix names the agent, navigation the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 导航的人；-or 后缀命名施动者，navigation 命名活动。

entries.definition: A country's fleet; it comes from navis too, but names the ships as an institution, not the act of steering them.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家的舰队；同样来自 navis，但把船只作为建制来命名，而非驾驶动作。

entries.definition: Guiding a vessel through a channel by landmarks; it is one branch of navigation, often close to shore.
entries.definitionCN: 凭地标引导船只通过航道；是导航的一支，常发生在近岸。

entries.definition: Finding one's way through a building or city, often by signs; navigation is broader and includes instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 在建筑或城市中认路，常靠标识；navigation 更宽，包含仪器。

entries.definition: Travelling and working at sea; it names a way of life, while navigation names the method.
entries.definitionCN: 在海上旅行与劳作；命名一种生活方式，而 navigation 命名方法。

entries.definition: Choosing the path for data or traffic; it is the technical descendant of route finding.
entries.definitionCN: 为数据或交通选择路径；是找路的技术后裔。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: navis 'ship' + agere 'drive' = drive a ship; the same two roots appear in navy and agent.
normal.cn: navis「船」+ agere「驾驶」= 驾船；同两个词根也出现在 navy 与 agent 中。

normal.en: The family runs navigate, navigator, navigational, navigable and navigability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 navigate、navigator、navigational、navigable 与 navigability。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: marine navigation, satellite navigation, a navigation system, inland navigation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：海上导航、卫星导航、导航系统、内河航运。

normal.en: Navigation answers two questions: where am I, and which way next.
normal.cn: 导航回答两个问题：我在哪里，下一步往哪。

normal.en: Website navigation borrows the sailor's chart: a menu is a map of pages.
normal.cn: 网页导航借用水手的海图：菜单就是页面的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a small boat with no land in sight, correcting its line by a single star.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看不见陆地的小船，靠一颗星修正航线。

abstract.en: Picture a menu bar as a row of harbour lights, each leading to one page.
abstract.cn: 想象菜单栏像一排港口灯，每盏通向一个页面。

abstract.en: Picture a monarch butterfly that has never seen the destination and still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一只从未见过目的地的帝王蝶，仍然抵达。

examples.en: Satellite navigation has replaced paper charts on many ships.
examples.cn: 卫星导航在许多船上取代了纸质海图。

examples.en: The site's navigation was redesigned so that new users could find the help page.
examples.cn: 网站导航经过重新设计，新用户能找到帮助页面。

examples.en: Inland navigation carries more freight than the nearby roads.
examples.cn: 内河航运运送的货物比附近公路更多。

dict_mnemonic.text: navy（船队）+ action（行动）——驾船找路的行动 → 航行、导航

root: 拉丁 navigatio「航行」← navigare「驾船」= navis（船）+ agere（驾驶）；与 navy、agent 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same loop of fix, compare and correct, but change the traveller: a hull, a walker, a mouse pointer, a butterfly, a spacecraft, an app, a barge and a student of the art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持「定位、比对、修正」的同一循环，只更换行者：船体、行人、鼠标指针、蝴蝶、航天器、应用、驳船，以及学习这门技艺的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: no shore in sight, one bearing checked again and again until the harbour appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见岸，反复校验一个方位，直到港口出现。

branches.en: THE ART: ship-driving as a practice and as a teachable body of knowledge.
branches.cn: 技艺：驾船既是一项实践，也是一套可教授的知识。

branches.en: THE LOOP: fix, compare, correct, whether by star, compass or ground signal.
branches.cn: 循环：定位、比对、修正，不论靠星辰、罗盘还是地面信号。

branches.en: NEW MEDIA: menus and satellite systems inherit the same chart and the same lost user.
branches.cn: 新媒介：菜单与卫星系统继承同样的海图与同样会迷路的使用者。

branches.en: WITHOUT INSTRUMENTS: the butterfly answers the two questions with senses only.
branches.cn: 无仪器：蝴蝶只靠感官回答那两个问题。

branches.en: COMMERCE: the old voyage becomes a transport mode measured in tonnage.
branches.cn: 商业：古老的航程变成以吨位计量的运输方式。

intro.en: Navigation is a Latin compound noun: navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive', then -atio. Both roots have large English families of their own.
intro.cn: navigation 是拉丁复合名词：navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」，再加 -atio。两个词根在英语中各自都有大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin navis 'ship' and agere 'drive' form navigare and navigatio; English draws navigate, navigator, navigable, navigational and navy from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 navis「船」与 agere「驾驶」构成 navigare 与 navigatio；英语由此得到 navigate、navigator、navigable、navigational 与 navy。

items.example: Navis is the source of navy and naval.
items.exampleCN: navis 是 navy 与 naval 的来源。

items.structure: agere, egi, actum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: Agere also gives agent and agenda.
items.exampleCN: agere 也生成 agent 与 agenda。

items.meaning: the act of sailing or finding a route
items.example: Navigation requires a fix and a course.
items.exampleCN: 导航需要一个定位与一条航线。
她驾船穿过狭窄的航道。

items.example: The navigator plotted the next leg.
items.exampleCN: 领航员标出了下一段航程。

items.meaning: able to be sailed or steered
items.example: The upper river is not navigable in winter.
items.exampleCN: 上游河道冬季不能通航。

items.example: Navigational aids were placed along the coast.
items.exampleCN: 沿海设置了一些导航设施。

items.meaning: a fleet, especially a war fleet

definition_zh: 海军；海军舰队；海军军种；藏青色；深蓝的
definition_en: a country's warships taken as a fighting force; the armed service that operates them; a very dark blue colour
core_image: 一排灰色军舰贴着码头停靠，桅杆上的旗在雾里慢慢升起
scene: 港口清晨起了雾，一排灰色军舰贴着码头停靠，桅杆上的旗还没升起。The navy kept the harbour closed until the fog lifted.
sceneCN: 这里是「海军舰队」（第 1 个义项：一国用于海上作战的舰船力量）；句意为雾散之前海军一直封锁着港口。图中可辨识物件：军舰、码头、雾、旗杆。

pos.zh: 海军；海军舰队；海军军种；藏青色

derivatives.zh: 由 navy 的词干与拉丁形容词词尾 -al 构成，义为「海军的；舰船的」
与 navy 同出拉丁词根 navis，义为「航行；导航」
由 navy 与 blue 复合而成，义为「藏青色；深蓝色」

senses.title: A country's warships as a fighting fleet
senses.titleCN: 海军舰队；一国的战舰力量
senses.definition: the warships of a country, considered together as a force that fights at sea
senses.definitionCN: 把一国的军舰作为一个整体来看，即用于海上作战的力量
senses.example: The navy sent two ships to guard the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 海军派出两艘军舰去守卫海峡。
senses.why: Latin navis meant ship, and Old French turned it into navie, a collective word for a body of ships; the English word still starts from the picture of many hulls moving together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 navis 意为船，古法语把它变成 navie，指成队的船；英语这个词的起点仍是许多船体一起移动的画面。

senses.title: The naval service as a branch of the armed forces
senses.definition: the organization, ships and people that a state maintains to fight at sea, one of its armed services
senses.definitionCN: 国家为海上作战而维持的机构、舰船与人员，是军种之一
senses.example: He joined the navy at eighteen and served for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他十八岁参加海军，服役十年。
senses.why: Once a fleet belongs to a state, it needs bases, ranks, pay and training; the name of the ships then passes to the institution that keeps them.
senses.whyCN: 当一支船队归国家所有，就需要基地、军衔、薪饷与训练；于是「船」的名字转而指维持这些船的机构。

senses.title: A very dark blue colour
senses.definition: a blue so dark that it looks almost black, used for uniforms and formal clothing
senses.definitionCN: 深到近乎黑色的蓝色，常用于制服与正式服装
senses.example: The curtains were a deep navy that made the room feel calm.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘是深沉的藏青色，让房间显得安静。
senses.why: Indigo dye held its colour in salt water, so naval cloth kept a depth that ordinary blue did not; when people needed a name for that particular dark blue, the uniform supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 靛蓝染料在海水里不易褪色，海军布料因此保住了寻常蓝色没有的深度；人们要给这种特定的深蓝起名时，制服就提供了一个现成的说法。

senses.title: Clothing in that dark blue shade
senses.definition: used of clothes, especially a dark blue that reads as almost black
senses.definitionCN: 用于衣物，尤指看起来近乎黑色的深蓝
senses.example: He wore a navy suit and a plain white shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿一套深蓝西装，配一件素白衬衫。
senses.why: Naval officers were long dressed in indigo cloth because the dye wore well at sea, so the colour of the uniform became a word for the colour itself, and then for clothes cut in it.
senses.whyCN: 海军军官长期穿靛蓝布料，因为这种染料在海上耐晒耐洗；制服的颜色于是成了颜色本身的名称，又进一步指用这种颜色做的衣服。

intro.en: Navy began as a French collective noun for a body of ships and only later attached itself to the warships of a state and to the colour of their cloth.
intro.cn: navy 最初是法语中表示「一队船」的集合名词，后来才附着到国家的战舰，以及战舰布料的那种颜色上。

items.en: Navis was the ordinary Latin word for a ship, and it stands behind naval, navigate and navy alike.
items.cn: navis 是拉丁语中表示「船」的常用词，naval、navigate 与 navy 都站在它后面。

items.en: Old French formed navie as a collective noun for a fleet, adding a group ending to the Latin stem for ship.
items.cn: 古法语用拉丁语「船」的词干加集合名词词尾，造出 navie，指一支船队。

items.en: Middle English borrowed navie as navy, still meaning a body of ships, whether for trade or for war.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 navie 写作 navy，仍指成队的船，商业与作战都可用。

items.en: With standing fleets and permanent admiralties, navy narrowed to the warships of the state, and naval uniforms gave the word a colour sense.
items.cn: 随着常备舰队与常设海军部出现，navy 收窄为国家战舰；海军制服又赋予这个词一层颜色义。

items.en: Modern English keeps the service, the fleet and the dark blue, and uses the adjective for suits and knitwear as readily as for warships.
items.cn: 现代英语保留军种、舰队与深蓝三义，形容词既可形容军舰，也可随口形容西装与针织衫。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words on the Latin stem for ship, including the adjective and the verb of sailing; the near-meaning group holds names for fleets and for the ships inside them.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「船」词干上的词，包括形容词与航行的动词；近义组收船队以及船队中各种船的名称。

entries.definition: Relating to a navy or to ships of war.
entries.definitionCN: 与海军或战舰有关的。

entries.definition: To work out a course and steer a ship or aircraft along it.
entries.definitionCN: 确定航线并驾驶船只或飞机前行。

entries.definition: The skill or process of finding a way across water or air.
entries.definitionCN: 在水上或空中确定方向的技能或过程。

entries.definition: The person who plots the course on a ship or plane.
entries.definitionCN: 在船上或飞机上负责确定航线的人。

entries.definition: A group of ships sailing or fighting together under one command.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一指挥下航行或作战的一群船。

entries.definition: A single ship built and armed for fighting at sea.
entries.definitionCN: 为海上作战而建造并武装的单艘船。

entries.definition: A large fleet of warships, especially the Spanish one of the sixteenth century.
entries.definitionCN: 庞大的战舰舰队，尤指十六世纪的西班牙无敌舰队。

entries.definition: Connected with the sea or with shipping, rather than with warships alone.
entries.definitionCN: 与海洋或航运有关，而不专指战舰。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin ship stem wearing a French collective ending, and its relatives all keep the image of hulls on water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「船」的词干披上法语的集合词尾，它的同族词都保留着水上船体的画面。

normal.en: Latin navis meant ship, so navy began as a crowd of ships rather than as an institution.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 navis 意为船，所以 navy 一开始是一群船，而不是一个机构。

normal.en: Old French navie turned the ship word into a collective, and English kept the shape but changed the ending to y.
normal.cn: 古法语 navie 把「船」这个词变成集合名词，英语保留了这个形状，只把词尾写成 y。

normal.en: Naval is navy plus the Latin adjective ending -al, and it describes anything belonging to a fleet.
normal.cn: naval 是 navy 加上拉丁语形容词词尾 -al，用来形容属于舰队的一切。

normal.en: Navigate is built on the same navis: a ship finding its way is the original picture behind navigation.

definition_zh: 附近的；邻近的；在附近；就近

scene: 傍晚的巷口，两棵梧桐树下摆着几张矮桌，邻居端着碗坐在门口。A nearby shop was still open, and the children ran in for sweets.
sceneCN: 这里是「附近的」（第 1 个义项：作形容词，指距离不远）；句意为附近那家小店还开着，孩子们跑进去买糖。图中可辨识物件：巷口、梧桐、矮桌、饭碗。

senses.title: Close to the place mentioned, before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for a place or thing that is only a short distance from the place being talked about
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词之前，指距离所说地点不远的地方或事物
senses.example: A nearby shop was still open, and the children ran in for sweets.
senses.exampleCN: 附近一家小店还开着，孩子们跑进去买糖。
senses.why: Near came from Old English neah, close at hand, and by from Old English bi, beside; putting them together produced a word whose whole job is to sit in front of a place and shorten the distance.
senses.whyCN: near 来自古英语 neah，意为「在手边」；by 来自古英语 bi，意为「在旁边」；两者合起来，造出一个专门放在地点名词前、把距离缩短的词。

senses.title: At a short distance away, after a verb
senses.definition: used after a verb or at the end of a clause to say that something happens a short distance from the place mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 放在动词之后或句末，表示事情发生在离所说地点不远的地方
senses.example: She lives nearby and walks over most mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 她住在附近，大多数早晨都走过来。
senses.why: English often lets a compound work as an adverb without any ending, so the same two prepositions that named a place beside another place also came to describe where an action happens.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让一个复合词不带词尾就直接作副词，于是原本用来说「在一个地点旁边的另一个地点」的两个介词，也用来描述动作发生在哪里。

intro.en: Nearby is a plain English compound of two Old English words for closeness, and it has been recorded only since the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: nearby 是两个表示「接近」的古英语词合成的普通英语复合词，有记录的历史只能追溯到十八世纪。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative near later became an ordinary adjective for what is not far.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级 near 后来变成普通形容词，表示「不远的」。

items.en: Bi meant beside, near or by the side of, and it survives in by, beside and the second half of nearby.
items.cn: bi 意为在旁边、靠近，它留在 by、beside 以及 nearby 的后半截里。

items.en: Middle English already paired near with by in phrases about standing or living close to a place.
items.cn: 中古英语已在表示「站在或住在某处近旁」的短语里把 near 与 by 配在一起。

items.en: The written compound nearby appears in the eighteenth century, first in American usage, and spreads in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 写成一个词的 nearby 在十八世纪出现，最早见于美国用法，十九世纪渐渐流行。

items.en: Modern English uses it both before nouns and after verbs, so one form covers two grammatical jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语让它既用于名词之前，也用于动词之后，同一个形式承担两种语法角色。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply near plus by, two old English words for closeness that fused into one adjective and adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 near 加 by，两个表示「接近」的古英语词合并成一个形容词兼副词。

normal.en: Old English neah meant close at hand, and by came from bi, beside; nearby is those two ideas welded together.
normal.cn: 古英语 neah 意为在手边，by 来自 bi（在旁边）；nearby 就是这两个意思焊在一起。

normal.en: The compound is written as one word, unlike the phrase near by, which still appears in older texts.
normal.cn: 这个复合词写成一个词，与旧文献里仍能见到的短语 near by 不同。

normal.en: Before a noun it is an adjective: a nearby town; after a verb it is an adverb: she lives nearby.
normal.cn: 放在名词前是形容词：a nearby town；放在动词后是副词：she lives nearby。

normal.en: Nearly looks like the same word with -ly, but it means almost, not at a short distance.
normal.cn: nearly 看起来只是加了 -ly，意思却是「几乎」，而不是「在不远处」。

normal.en: Nearness is the noun made with -ness, useful when the sentence needs a subject rather than a place.
normal.cn: nearness 是用 -ness 构成的名词，句子需要一个主语而不是地点时就用它。

abstract.en: Two short words for standing beside something can do the work of a whole phrase about distance.
abstract.cn: 两个表示「站在旁边」的短词，就能顶替一整句关于距离的描述。

abstract.en: A word that only shortens distance shows how much English trusts a compound to do a preposition's job.
abstract.cn: 一个只负责缩短距离的词，说明英语多么信任复合词去承担介词的工作。

abstract.en: What is nearby is not yet reached, which is why the word always leaves a small gap open.
abstract.cn: 「附近的」东西还没有被走到，所以这个词总留着一小段没走完的距离。

senses.title: Almost, but not completely
senses.definition: not quite true or not quite done, though very close to it
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近，但还没有完全达到或完成
senses.example: I nearly missed the last train because the lift was slow.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯太慢，我差一点错过末班车。
senses.why: Near began as a word for physical closeness, and the ending -ly first meant in a close manner; spoken English then stretched that short gap from space into degree, so a thing that is close to happening becomes nearly happening.
senses.whyCN: near 原本表示空间上的接近，词尾 -ly 最初意为「以接近的方式」；口语把这个小缝隙从空间拉到位次，于是「接近发生」的事就成了「几乎发生」。

senses.title: Very close to a stated amount or time
senses.titleCN: 将近；差不多（数量或时间）
senses.definition: used before figures and periods to say that the real amount is a little below the one named
senses.definitionCN: 放在数字与时间段之前，表示实际数量略低于所说的那个数
senses.example: Nearly a thousand people came to the opening.
senses.exampleCN: 将近一千人参加了开幕式。
senses.why: Measuring a short distance and measuring a small shortfall use the same picture, so the word that once said two places are close now says a total is close to a round figure.
senses.whyCN: 量一小段距离与量一小点差额用的是同一幅画面，于是那个原本说「两地相近」的词，现在说「总数接近某个整数」。

senses.title: Closely, in family connections
senses.titleCN: 密切地；亲近地（指亲属关系）
senses.definition: used with related or connected to mean closely, chiefly in older or careful English
senses.definitionCN: 与 related 等词连用表示「关系密切」，多见于较旧或较正式的英语
senses.example: The two families were nearly related by marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个家庭因婚姻而关系很近。
senses.why: The older sense of the adverb was simply closely, and kinship is where that sense survives; the everyday sense moved away to almost, leaving this use behind like a fossil.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词较早的意思就是「紧密地」，亲属关系正是这层意思的留存处；日常义漂向「几乎」，把这一用法像化石一样留在了原地。

intro.en: Nearly is near plus the old adverb ending, and its meaning drifted from closely to almost while one formal use kept the older sense.
intro.cn: nearly 是 near 加旧副词词尾，词义从「紧密地」漂到「几乎」，只有一种正式用法保留了旧义。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative gave English the form near that nearly is built on.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级给英语提供了 near 这个形式，nearly 就建在它上面。

items.en: The ending -lice meant in the manner of, and it is the ancestor of the modern -ly in nearly and other adverbs.
items.cn: -lice 意为「以……的方式」，是现代副词词尾 -ly 的前身，nearly 等词都用它。

items.en: Middle English ner meant both near and closely, and the new adverb nerliche carried the sense of closely, carefully.
items.cn: 中古英语 ner 兼有「近」与「紧密」两义，新的副词 nerliche 表示「紧密地、仔细地」。

items.en: The adverb is recorded in the sixteenth century; by the seventeenth the sense almost is common in speech and in print.
items.cn: 这个副词在十六世纪见于记录；到十七世纪，「几乎」义已在口语与书面语中常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps almost as the main sense, adds the counting use before numbers, and retains closely only in phrases about kinship.
items.cn: 现代英语以「几乎」为主义，又添上数字前的计量用法，只在与亲属关系有关的短语里保留「密切地」。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the root and the forms built directly on it; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs that stop just short of a fact.
note.cn: 形近组收词根以及直接建在词根上的形式；近义组收其他表示「差一点、差不多」的副词。

entries.definition: Not far away, in space, time or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 空间、时间或程度上不远的。

entries.definition: The quality of being close, made with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的「接近、临近」这一性质。

entries.definition: The comparative of near, for a smaller distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的比较级，表示更近的距离。

entries.definition: The superlative of near, for the smallest distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的最高级，表示最近的距离。

entries.definition: Very close to, and often interchangeable with nearly before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 非常接近，在动词前常可与 nearly 互换。

entries.definition: In effect, though not strictly true; stronger in speech than nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上差不多，口语中语气比 nearly 更强。

entries.definition: Almost entirely, used of conditions rather than of counted things.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎完全，多用于状态而非可数之物。

entries.definition: About, allowing for a margin on either side rather than falling short.
entries.definitionCN: 大约，允许上下浮动，而不专指不足。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic root for closeness with an old adverb ending, and its main sense has slid from manner into degree.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语「接近」词根加旧副词词尾，主义从「方式」滑到了「程度」。

normal.en: Near means close, and -ly once meant in that manner, so nearly first described how something was done, not how complete it was.
normal.cn: near 意为近，-ly 原表示「以那种方式」，所以 nearly 最初描述的是做法，而不是完成程度。

normal.en: Before a verb, nearly and almost usually exchange freely: I nearly fell, I almost fell.
normal.cn: 在动词前，nearly 与 almost 通常可以互换：I nearly fell 与 I almost fell 意思相同。

normal.en: Before a number, nearly means a little below it; about or approximately allows the figure to be above as well.
normal.cn: 在数字前，nearly 表示略低于该数；about 或 approximately 则允许高于该数。

normal.en: Not nearly is a fixed phrase of strong denial: the job is not nearly finished means it is far from finished.
normal.cn: not nearly 是语气很强的固定说法：「the job is not nearly finished」意为「离完成还差得远」。

normal.en: Nearly related keeps the old sense of closely, which is why it sounds formal beside the everyday almost.
normal.cn: nearly related 保留了「密切」的旧义，所以它放在日常的 almost 旁边会显得正式。

abstract.en: A closing door measured in half steps shows how English turns a gap in space into a gap in degree.
abstract.cn: 用半步来量的合上的车门，说明英语怎样把空间里的缝隙变成程度上的缝隙。

abstract.en: The same word can fall just short of a train and just short of a thousand, because counting is only measuring with numbers.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以差一点赶上车，也可以差一点到一千，因为计数不过是拿数字来量。

abstract.en: A fossil sense survives in family talk, reminding us that nearly once meant tightly, not almost.
abstract.cn: 一个化石般的旧义活在亲属称谓里，提醒人 nearly 曾经意为「紧紧地」，而不是「几乎」。

examples.en: The bottle is nearly empty; we need another.
examples.cn: 瓶子快空了，我们得再拿一瓶。

examples.en: She has worked here for nearly twenty years.
examples.cn: 她在这里工作了将近二十年。

examples.en: It was nearly midnight when the phone rang.
examples.cn: 电话响的时候已将近午夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔利」——差一步就到「near」，可惜还没到；nearly 就是几乎、差一点。

root: 古英语 neah（近）的比较级 near，加副词词尾 -lice（现代 -ly）构成；属日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small remaining gap; it can be a gap before an event, a gap below a number, or the old gap of close kinship.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「剩下的一小段差距」；它可以是事件之前的差距、数字以下的差距，也可以是旧义里亲属之间的贴近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a train door sliding shut while one foot is still half a step from the step.
core.cn: 核心意象：车门正在合上，一只脚离踏板还差半步。

branches.en: a hand reaching a door as it closes
branches.cn: 车门合上时伸过去的手

branches.en: a platform emptying after the last announcement
branches.cn: 最后一次广播后渐渐空去的站台

branches.en: a hall filled just short of a thousand
branches.cn: 坐得差一点满一千人的大厅

branches.en: a guest list counted twice at a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼上数了两遍的宾客名单

branches.en: two families joined by one marriage
branches.cn: 因一桩婚姻连在一起的两家人

intro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective of closeness, an Old English adverb ending, and the modern shapes of both.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语表示「接近」的形容词、一个古英语副词词尾，以及两者在现代的形式构成。

latinIntro.en: Nearly belongs to the Germanic family of near, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: nearly 属于 near 这一日耳曼语词族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: tidy and in good order; simple and skilfully done; drunk without ice or water; small and well shaped
core_image: 桌面上书本按高矮排成一线，笔尖都朝同一个方向
scene: 宿舍的桌上，书本按高矮排成一线，几支笔都朝同一个方向摆着。His desk stayed neat even during the exam week.
sceneCN: 这里是「整洁的」（第 1 个义项：摆放有序、不凌乱）；句意为即便在考试周，他的书桌也保持整洁。图中可辨识物件：书桌、书本、笔。

senses.title: Tidy and in good order
senses.definition: arranged carefully, with everything in its place and no clutter
senses.definitionCN: 摆放得仔细，各在其位，没有杂乱
senses.example: His desk stayed neat even during the exam week.
senses.exampleCN: 即便在考试周，他的书桌也保持整洁。
senses.why: The word came into English from French net, clean and bright, and its first job was to describe a surface with nothing spoiling it; order was the visible proof of that cleanliness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法语 net 进入英语，本义是「干净、明亮」，最初形容没有污损的表面；整齐有序就是这种干净看得见的证据。

senses.title: Simple and skilfully done
senses.titleCN: 简洁巧妙的；干净利落的
senses.definition: done with care and skill so that the result is simple, exact and easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: 做得细致而有技巧，结果简单、准确、容易把握
senses.example: She found a neat solution that saved everyone an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出一个简洁的办法，给每个人省下一小时。
senses.why: A surface is neat when nothing extra is on it, and a plan is neat when nothing extra is in it; the same dislike of clutter moves from tables to arguments.
senses.whyCN: 表面整洁是因为上面没有多余的东西，方案简洁是因为里面没有多余的步骤；同一种对杂乱的排斥，从桌面移到了论证里。

senses.title: Drunk plain, without ice or water
senses.definition: used of strong drink served on its own, with nothing added
senses.definitionCN: 用于烈酒，指单喝、不兑任何东西
senses.example: He asked for a neat whisky and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯不加冰的威士忌，坐在窗边。
senses.why: A glass with nothing added is clean in the same literal way, so the old adjective for an unspoiled surface was applied to a drink that has not been diluted.
senses.whyCN: 什么都没加的杯子，字面上同样「干净」，于是那个形容未受污损表面的旧形容词，被用到了没有兑水的酒上。

senses.title: Small, trim and well shaped
senses.definition: used of a person's body or build, meaning small, compact and pleasing in shape
senses.definitionCN: 用于人的身材，意为小巧、紧凑、比例好看
senses.example: The dancer had a neat figure and very straight posture.
senses.exampleCN: 那位舞者身材小巧匀称，姿态非常挺拔。
senses.why: A small object with clean lines looks finished rather than cramped, so neat came to praise a body built on a small scale but without awkwardness.
senses.whyCN: 线条干净的小物件看起来是完成品，而不是被挤小的；于是 neat 也用来称赞小巧却不显笨拙的身材。

intro.en: Neat came through French from a Latin adjective for something shining and polished, and English widened it from a clean surface to a clear plan and an undiluted drink.
intro.cn: neat 经法语来自一个表示「光亮、打磨过」的拉丁形容词，英语把它的词义从干净表面扩展到清晰方案与不兑水的酒。

items.en: Nitidus meant shining, bright and polished, and by extension elegant and refined in appearance.
items.cn: nitidus 意为光亮的、鲜明的、打磨过的，引申指外表雅致、精致。

items.en: The verb nitere meant to shine or to look bright, and it is the source of the adjective and of the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 nitere 意为发光、显得明亮，是这个形容词以及整族词的来源。

items.en: Old French net kept the sense of clean, clear and unspoiled, and dropped the Latin brightness into a plainer cleanliness.
items.cn: 古法语 net 保留「干净、清澈、未受污损」的意思，把拉丁语的「光亮」落成了更朴素的「干净」。

items.en: Middle English nete or neat described clean clothes, clear writing and a person who kept things in order.
items.cn: 中古英语 nete 或 neat 形容干净的衣服、清楚的字迹，以及把东西收拾得井井有条的人。

items.en: Modern English adds the praise of a simple plan, the serving of undiluted spirits and the description of a compact figure.
items.cn: 现代英语添上对简洁方案的称赞、对不兑水烈酒的用法，以及对小巧身材的描述。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adverb, the noun and the verb built on neat; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for order and for a well-kept appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收由 neat 构成的副词、名词与动词；近义组收表示「有序」与「外表收拾得好」的形容词。

entries.definition: In a tidy or skilful way, made with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以整齐或利落的方式；由 neat 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being tidy or skilfully simple.
entries.definitionCN: 整洁或简洁巧妙的性质。

entries.definition: To make something tidy, formed with -en.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物收拾整齐；由 neat 加 -en 构成。

entries.definition: A mesh for catching things; only the spelling is close to neat.
entries.definitionCN: 用来捕捉东西的网；只是拼写与 neat 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Arranged with everything in place, often said of rooms and habits.
entries.definitionCN: 各物归位、摆放有序，常用于房间与习惯。

entries.definition: Following a clear arrangement or method, often of groups and procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循清楚的安排或方法，多用于群体与程序。

entries.definition: Neat and well shaped, especially of a person or a garden.
entries.definitionCN: 整齐而外形好看，尤指人或花园。

entries.definition: Smart and clean in appearance, usually of a person dressed well.
entries.definitionCN: 外表利落干净，通常指穿着得体的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a French cleaning word with a Latin shine behind it, and its senses all keep some idea of nothing extra.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语中表示「干净」的词，背后有拉丁语的「光亮」，各个义项都带着「没有多余之物」的意思。

normal.en: French net meant clean and bright, and English kept the meaning but changed the spelling to neat.
normal.cn: 法语 net 意为干净、明亮，英语保留了意思，只把拼写改成 neat。

normal.en: Latin nitidus, shining, stands behind the French word, so neat and nitid share one old picture of a polished surface.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nitidus（光亮的）站在法语词背后，所以 neat 与 nitid 共享一幅打磨过的表面画面。

normal.en: Neatly is the adverb, neatness the noun, neaten the verb; the family adds endings rather than new stems.
normal.cn: neatly 是副词，neatness 是名词，neaten 是动词；这一族只加词尾，不换词干。

normal.en: A neat solution is praised for having no extra steps, which is the same judgement as a neat desk with no extra papers.
normal.cn: a neat solution 被称赞是因为没有多余步骤，这与「没有多余纸张的整洁书桌」是同一种判断。

normal.en: Neat whisky has nothing added, so the clean-surface sense survives most literally in the glass.
normal.cn: neat whisky 什么都不加，所以「干净表面」这层意思在酒杯里保留得最字面。

abstract.en: Cleanliness, brightness and order turn out to be three views of one surface with nothing on it that should not be there.
abstract.cn: 干净、光亮与有序，其实只是同一个表面的三个视角：上面没有不该有的东西。

abstract.en: A word that began by praising a polished table ends up praising a proof with no wasted line.
abstract.cn: 一个从称赞打磨过的桌面开始的词，最后用来称赞没有一句废话的证明。

abstract.en: Serving a drink neat is the same compliment as keeping a desk neat: nothing has been added.
abstract.cn: 把酒纯着端上来，与把桌子收拾整齐是同一种称赞：什么都没有往里加。

examples.en: Her handwriting is small and very neat.
examples.cn: 她的字小而工整。

examples.en: He keeps his tools in a neat row on the shelf.
examples.cn: 他把工具在架子上排成整齐的一列。

examples.en: The team needed a neat way to explain the result.
examples.cn: 团队需要一个简洁的方式来解释这个结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼特」——东西摆得利落，一眼看过去清清爽爽；neat 就是整洁的。

root: 古法语 net（干净、明亮）来自拉丁语 nitidus（光亮的），一般认为与动词 nitere（发光）同源；本义「干净明亮」，后引申出整洁、简洁、纯饮与小巧诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a surface with nothing extra on it; order, simplicity, an undiluted drink and a compact figure are four ways that emptiness of extras shows itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有多余之物的表面」；有序、简洁、不兑水的酒与小巧的身材，是这种「无多余」显现出来的四种方式。

definition_en: in a way that leaves everything tidy and in place; skilfully and with precision; briefly and clearly

scene: 衣柜的抽屉拉开，衬衫按颜色叠成方块，袜子卷成同样大小的卷。She neatly folded the sheets and stacked them on the shelf.

senses.title: In a tidy and orderly way
senses.definition: in a way that puts everything in its proper place and leaves no clutter
senses.definitionCN: 以各物归位、不留杂乱的方式做事
senses.example: She neatly folded the sheets and stacked them on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 她把床单叠得整整齐齐，摞在架子上。
senses.why: Neat describes the finished state of a surface, and the ending -ly turns that state into the manner of the action that produced it, so neatly always points at how the hands worked.
senses.whyCN: neat 描述表面的完成状态，词尾 -ly 把这种状态变成造成它的动作方式，所以 neatly 总是指向双手怎么做的。

senses.title: Skilfully and with precision
senses.definition: in a careful, exact and efficient way, so that the result looks effortless and simple
senses.definitionCN: 以细致、准确、高效的方式，使结果显得轻松而简单
senses.example: He neatly solved the problem in three lines.
senses.exampleCN: 他用三行就干净利落地解决了这个问题。
senses.why: When a task is done with nothing wasted, the result has the same bare cleanness as a tidy desk, so the adverb of order also praises economy of effort.
senses.whyCN: 一件事做得没有半点浪费，结果就带着和整洁桌面一样的干净，于是这个表示「有序」的副词也用来称赞省力。

senses.title: Briefly and clearly
senses.definition: in a short and well-organized way, used of speech, writing or a summary
senses.definitionCN: 以简短而有条理的方式，用于说话、写作或概述
senses.example: The report neatly sums up a year of work in two pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告用两页纸把一年的工作简明扼要地总结了。
senses.why: Writing that keeps only what is needed looks like a room with only what is needed, so neatly moves from furniture to sentences without changing its judgement.
senses.whyCN: 只留下必需内容的文章，看起来就像只摆必需家具的房间，于是 neatly 从家具移到句子，判断标准却一点没变。

intro.en: Neatly is the adjective of cleanliness turned into an adverb of manner, and its history is the history of neat plus the English -ly.
intro.cn: neatly 是把表示「干净」的形容词变成方式副词的产物，它的历史就是 neat 加上英语词尾 -ly 的历史。

items.en: Nitidus meant shining and polished, and it reached French with the sense of something clean and unspoiled.
items.cn: nitidus 意为光亮、打磨过的，传到法语时带着「干净、未受损」的意思。

items.en: Old French net described clean cloth, clear writing and a neat appearance, and English borrowed it in that shape.
items.cn: 古法语 net 形容干净的布、清楚的字迹与整洁的外表，英语就是照这个形态借入的。

items.en: Middle English neat named the quality of a well-kept thing, and the adverb was formed by adding the ending for manner.
items.cn: 中古英语 neat 指收拾得好的事物所具有的性质，副词则由加上表示方式的词尾构成。

items.en: The old ending -lice became -ly, and it turned adjectives of state into adverbs of how an action is carried out.
items.cn: 旧词尾 -lice 变成 -ly，把表示状态的形容词变成说明动作如何进行的副词。

items.en: Modern English uses neatly for folding, dressing, writing and solving, keeping one adverb for every kind of visible order.
items.cn: 现代英语把 neatly 用于叠衣、穿衣、书写与解题，各种看得见的秩序都用同一个副词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds neat and the words formed on it; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs of careful, orderly execution.
note.cn: 形近组收 neat 以及建在它上面的词；近义组收其他表示「仔细、有序地做事」的副词。

entries.definition: Tidy, simple or undiluted, the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 整洁的、简洁的或纯的，是副词背后的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality that neatly describes when it appears in an action.
entries.definitionCN: neatly 所描述的那种性质本身。

entries.definition: To make something tidy, formed with -en.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物收拾整齐；由 neat 加 -en 构成。

entries.definition: Shining and polished, a learned word from the same Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 光亮而打磨过的，是同出拉丁形容词的书面罕用词。

entries.definition: With everything put away, said of rooms and possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西都收好，多用于房间与物品。

entries.definition: Without mess or awkwardness, often of a cut or a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不拖泥带水，常用于切口或动作。

entries.definition: With exact measurement or exact wording, stressing accuracy.
entries.definitionCN: 以精确的度量或措辞，强调准确。

entries.definition: Step by step in a fixed order, stressing the plan rather than the look.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定顺序一步步来，强调计划而非外观。

normalIntro.en: The word is neat with the manner ending -ly, so it names the way an action produces order rather than the order itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 neat 加表示方式的词尾 -ly，所以它命名的是动作造成秩序的方式，而不是秩序本身。

normal.en: Neat is the adjective and neatly the adverb: a neat shelf, but she stacked them neatly.
normal.cn: neat 是形容词，neatly 是副词：说 a neat shelf，但说 she stacked them neatly。

normal.en: The ending -ly goes back to Old English -lice, which meant in the manner of.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 可追到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。

normal.en: Neatly keeps the clean-surface idea of neat, so a neatly solved problem has no wasted steps.
normal.cn: neatly 保留了 neat 的「干净表面」之意，所以 a neatly solved problem 没有多余步骤。

normal.en: Neatly folded and neatly dressed both describe how the result looks to someone standing nearby.
normal.cn: neatly folded 与 neatly dressed 都在描述结果在旁人眼里是什么样子。

normal.en: In writing, neatly means briefly and in order, the same standard applied to sentences instead of shelves.
normal.cn: 在写作里，neatly 意为简短而有条理，只是把同一标准从架子用到句子上。

abstract.en: An adverb of tidiness is really a report on the hands: it says the work left nothing loose behind.
abstract.cn: 一个表示整洁的副词，其实是对双手的报告：它说这件活没留下任何松散之处。

abstract.en: Order can be folded into a drawer, solved on a blackboard, or compressed into two pages, and the same word follows it.
abstract.cn: 秩序可以叠进抽屉、写在黑板上，也可以压进两页纸，同一个词一路跟着它。

abstract.en: Neatly is neat seen from the side of the action, which is why it always answers the question of how.
abstract.cn: neatly 是从动作那一侧看到的 neat，所以它回答的总是「怎么做」。

examples.en: The towels were neatly stacked in the cupboard.
examples.cn: 毛巾整齐地摞在柜子里。

examples.en: She neatly avoided the question and moved on.
examples.cn: 她巧妙地避开那个问题，继续往下说。

examples.en: Everything on the desk was neatly arranged by size.
examples.cn: 桌上的每样东西都按大小排列得整整齐齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼特利」——手脚利落，东西摆得整齐；neatly 就是整齐地。

root: 由 neat（整洁的，源自法语 net、拉丁语 nitidus）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；本义「以干净整洁的方式」，后引申出「利落地」「简洁地」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the manner of producing order; folding, solving and writing are three places where that manner can be seen.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「造成秩序的方式」；叠衣、解题与写作，是这种方式可以显现的三个场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shirts folded into identical squares and laid in layers inside a drawer.
core.cn: 核心意象：衬衫叠成同样大小的方块，一层层放进抽屉。

branches.en: sheets folded into one flat stack
branches.cn: 叠成一摞平整的床单

branches.en: socks rolled to the same size
branches.cn: 卷成同样大小的袜子

branches.en: three lines that finish a long proof
branches.cn: 三行就结束的冗长证明

branches.en: a problem closed without a stray mark
branches.cn: 做完后没有多余笔迹的题

branches.en: two pages that hold a whole year
branches.cn: 两页纸装下一整年

intro.en: The word is the cleanliness adjective of French and Latin origin plus the English manner ending that turned it into an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是源自法语与拉丁语、表示「干净」的形容词，加上把它变成副词的英语方式词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin nitidus and its verb nitere stand behind the French adjective, and the English adverb adds only a manner ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nitidus 及其动词 nitere 位于法语形容词之后，英语副词只再加一个方式词尾。

items.meaning: in a tidy or skilful way

latinEntries.meaningCN: 光亮的；打磨过的；整洁的

definition_zh: 必然地；必定；不可避免地；不一定（用于 not necessarily）
definition_en: in a way that cannot be avoided or that follows with logical certainty; also used in the phrase not necessarily to deny that something is always true
core_image: 一条被两端拉紧的锁链，中间没有可以退让的余地
scene: 山道上的碎石还湿着，跑得太急的人收不住脚，一定会摔下去。If you run down a wet slope, you will necessarily fall.
sceneCN: 这里「necessarily」是「必然地、必定」（第 1 个义项：由逻辑或事实逼出来的结果）；句意是跑下湿滑斜坡的人必然会摔倒。图中可辨识物件：湿漉漉的碎石、斜坡、收不住的脚步。

pos.zh: 必然地；必定；不可避免地

derivatives.zh: 与 necessarily 同出于拉丁 necessarius，义为「必要的；必然的」
由拉丁 necessitas 进入英语，义为「必要性；必然性」
由 necessity 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「使成为必要」

senses.title: As a logical certainty
senses.definition: in a way that follows by logic, so that no other result is possible
senses.definitionCN: 按逻辑推演下来必然如此，不可能有别的结果
senses.example: A triangle necessarily has three sides.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形必然有三条边。
senses.why: Latin necesse joined ne, not, with cedere, to give way: what cannot give way cannot be escaped, so the adverb states a result that logic or fact forces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 necesse 把「不」与「退让」拼在一起：不肯退让的东西就躲不开，所以这个副词说的是逻辑或事实逼出来的结果。

senses.title: In every case, without exception
senses.titleCN: 不可避免地；每次都如此
senses.definition: in a way that happens in all cases, because the circumstances leave no room for an alternative
senses.definitionCN: 在所有情形下都会发生，因为客观条件没有留下别的可能
senses.example: When demand outruns supply, prices necessarily rise.
senses.exampleCN: 当需求超过供给，价格必然上涨。
senses.why: The same picture of a chain with no slack moves from one deduction to a general rule: once the conditions hold, the outcome cannot be held back.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「锁链没有余量」的画面，从单次推论扩展到普遍规律：条件一旦成立，结果就压不住。

senses.title: Not in every case, in the phrase not necessarily
senses.definition: used after not to say that something is possible but not always or not certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 用在 not 之后，表示某事有可能，但并非总是或并非一定成立
senses.example: A quiet student is not necessarily a bored one.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的学生不一定就是觉得无聊。
senses.why: Negating a word of absolute certainty leaves a deliberate gap: the link may hold sometimes, but it is not forced, so the phrase warns against a hasty conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 把表示绝对必然的词一否定，就留下一个刻意的空隙：这种联系有时成立，却不是被逼出来的，所以这个说法是在提醒人别急着下结论。

intro.en: Necessarily is the adverb built on necessary, and the two words share one Latin idea: a necessity that cannot be pushed aside.
intro.cn: necessarily 是由 necessary 加 -ly 构成的副词，两词共享同一个拉丁观念：一种推不开的必然。

items.en: A negative particle and a root for yielding are generally reconstructed behind the Latin family, though the exact earlier shape is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语这一族词的背后有一个否定小词和一个表示「退让」的词根，但更早的具体形式仍有争议。

items.en: Latin necesse meant unavoidable or inevitable; a common account reads it as ne, not, plus cedere, to give way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 necesse 意为不可避免、必然；一种常见解释是 ne（不）加 cedere（退让）。

items.en: The adjective necessarius described what one cannot do without, carrying the idea of an unyielding necessity into everyday need.
items.cn: 形容词 necessarius 描述离不开的东西，把「不肯退让的必然」带进了日常的「需要」。

items.en: Middle English used necessarie for what must be, and the adverb grew beside it with the ending -ly.
items.cn: 中古英语用 necessarie 表示「必须如此的」，副词形式随后加 -ly 长出来。

items.en: Modern English keeps necessarily for logical and practical certainty, and the negative phrase not necessarily for the deliberate exception.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 necessarily 表示逻辑与事实上的确定，并用否定短语 not necessarily 表示刻意留下的例外。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family and its English endings; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of certainty and of unavoidable occurrence.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁词族与英语词尾展开；近义组收表示确定与不可避免发生的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb, meaning needed or certain.
entries.definitionCN: 副词背后的形容词，义为「必要的；必然的」。

entries.definition: The state or quality of being necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 必要性；必然性。

entries.definition: To make something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要。

entries.definition: In a way that is not needed.
entries.definitionCN: 以不必要的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be prevented.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免地；终究会。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be escaped.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免地。

entries.definition: Without doubt; for sure.
entries.definitionCN: 无疑地；肯定地。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin refusal to budge, and its family keeps turning that refusal into logical certainty and practical necessity.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「不肯让步」的劲头，同族词不断把这种不肯让步变成逻辑上的确定与现实中的必需。

normal.en: Necesse is read as ne plus cedere, so the core picture is something that will not give way.
normal.cn: necesse 可拆成 ne 加 cedere，核心画面就是一件不肯退让的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective necessary into the adverb necessarily, just as it turns quick into quickly.
normal.cn: -ly 把形容词 necessary 变成副词 necessarily，就像把 quick 变成 quickly。

normal.en: Not necessarily does not cancel the word; it denies that the link holds in every case.
normal.cn: not necessarily 并没有取消这个词，它否认的是这种联系在每种情况下都成立。

normal.en: Necessity and necessitate are relatives: one names the state, the other the act of making something necessary.
normal.cn: necessity 与 necessitate 是同族词：一个指状态，一个指使某事成为必要的动作。

normal.en: In a proof, necessarily marks the step that no counterexample can overturn.
normal.cn: 在证明里，necessarily 标出的是任何反例都推不翻的那一步。

abstract.en: A chain tightened at both ends is a good picture of a conclusion that cannot be loosened by argument.
abstract.cn: 两端拉紧的锁链，很适合形容一个怎么争辩都松不开的结论。

abstract.en: The negative phrase works like a small door left open in an otherwise closed wall.
abstract.cn: 那个否定短语就像一堵封闭的墙上故意留下的一扇小门。

abstract.en: Every time the word appears, someone is claiming that the room for choice has shrunk to nothing.
abstract.cn: 这个词每次出现，都有人在声称可供选择的空间已经缩到没有。

examples.en: A triangle necessarily has three sides.
examples.cn: 三角形必然有三条边。

examples.en: When demand outruns supply, prices necessarily rise.
examples.cn: 当需求超过供给，价格必然上涨。

examples.en: A quiet student is not necessarily a bored one.
examples.cn: 安静的学生不一定就是觉得无聊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢色塞热利」——听着像一串含糊的尾音，意思却是躲不开的必然；记住 necessarily 是必然地。

root: 拉丁语 necesse（不可避免）一般认为由否定成分 ne- 与 cedere（退让）构成；加 -arius 得 necessarius，再加 -ly 成为 necessarily。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a necessity that will not yield; the senses divide into logical certainty, universal occurrence, and the negated phrase that keeps one exception alive.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种不肯退让的必然；义项分出逻辑上的确定、普遍发生的情形，以及保留一个例外的否定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain pulled tight at both ends, with no slack left in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条两端拉紧的锁链，中间不留一点余量。

branches.en: a proof that closes every other door one by one
branches.cn: 证明把其他可能的门一扇扇关掉

branches.en: three sides that cannot be counted otherwise
branches.cn: 三条边怎么数都改不了

branches.en: a price climbing because supply has run short
branches.cn: 供给短缺，价格随之上抬

branches.en: a calm face read as boredom without proof
branches.cn: 凭一张平静的脸就断定人家无聊

branches.en: a question answered with a careful maybe
branches.cn: 一个问题只得到谨慎的「也许」

intro.en: One Latin adjective of necessity, its negative and verbal parts, and two English endings hold this entry together.
intro.cn: 一个表示必然的拉丁形容词、它的否定与动词成分，以及两个英语词尾共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the whole family: necesse, its adjective necessarius and the verb cedere behind the negative element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了整族词：necesse、它的形容词 necessarius，以及藏在否定成分背后的动词 cedere。

definition_zh: 必要的；必需的；必然的；必需品（常用复数 necessaries）
definition_en: needed so that something can be done or achieved; certain to happen as a result; and, as a plural noun, the things a person needs
core_image: 一把钥匙插进锁孔，门后是缺了它就办不成的那件事
scene: 出发前一晚，队长把清单摊在木桌上逐项核对，缺了任何一样队伍都走不成。A map and a compass are necessary for the route they have chosen.
sceneCN: 这里「necessary」是「必要的、必需的」（第 1 个义项：缺了就无法完成某事）；句意是地图和指南针是他们所选路线必需的装备。图中可辨识物件：木桌上的清单、地图、指南针。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 necessitas 进入英语，义为「必要性；必然性；必需品」
由 necessary 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「必然地」
由 necessary 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不必要的」

senses.title: Needed for a purpose
senses.definition: required so that something can happen or be achieved
senses.definitionCN: 为了做成某事而不可缺少的
senses.example: Water is necessary for every living cell.
senses.exampleCN: 水对每个活细胞来说都是必需的。
senses.why: Latin necessarius first meant what cannot be avoided; English moved that force into the practical sphere, where it marks what cannot be left out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 necessarius 最初指躲不开的东西；英语把这份强制感移进日常事务，用来标出不能漏掉的那一项。

senses.title: Certain to follow as a result
senses.definition: certain to happen as a result of something else, with no real alternative
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的结果必定发生，没有别的可能
senses.example: A rise in temperature is a necessary result of the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 温度上升是这场反应的必然结果。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, it can also be called necessary as a consequence: the cause leaves the effect no room to differ.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既躲不开，也就可以作为结果被称为必然：原因没给结果留下任何差异的余地。

senses.title: Things a person cannot do without
senses.definition: the items a person needs for daily life, usually used in the plural form
senses.definitionCN: 日常生活离不开的物品，通常用复数形式
senses.example: The family packed only the necessaries for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人只收拾了过冬最基本的必需品。
senses.why: An adjective turns into a noun when English wants to name the objects that carry the quality; the plural marks a set of such objects rather than one.
senses.whyCN: 当英语想直接称呼带有这种性质的物件时，形容词就变成名词；复数标记的是一整套这样的东西，而不是单件。

intro.en: Necessary reached English through French from Latin, and its root idea is not simply wanted but impossible to avoid.
intro.cn: necessary 经法语从拉丁语进入英语，它的根义不是「想要」，而是「避不开」。

items.en: Behind the Latin word lie a negative particle and a root for yielding, though the exact prehistoric form is not settled.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词的背后有一个否定小词和一个表示退让的词根，但更早的确切形式尚无定论。

items.en: Latin necesse meant unavoidable; one widely repeated account divides it into ne, not, and cedere, to give way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 necesse 意为不可避免；一种流传很广的解释把它分成 ne（不）与 cedere（退让）。

items.en: The adjective necessarius described what one cannot do without and passed both necessity and practical need to later languages.
items.cn: 形容词 necessarius 指离不开的东西，把「必然」与「实际需要」一起传给了后世语言。

items.en: Old French necessaire carried the word to England after the Norman conquest, where it was spelled in several ways.
items.cn: 古法语 necessaire 在诺曼征服后把这个词带到英格兰，当时拼写有好几种。

items.en: Modern English uses necessary for what is required and for what must follow, and the plural noun for the bare items of daily life.
items.cn: 现代英语用 necessary 既指「必需」也指「必然」，复数名词则指日常生活里最基本的那些东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same Latin stem and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what cannot be done without.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一拉丁词干及其词尾展开；近义组收表示「缺了就不行」的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb formed from necessary with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 由 necessary 加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The state of being necessary, or a thing that is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 必要性；必需品。

entries.definition: To make something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要。

entries.definition: Not needed; more than is required.
entries.definitionCN: 不必要的；多余的。

entries.definition: Absolutely needed for something to exist or work.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在或运作绝对需要的。

entries.definition: Needed for life or for success.
entries.definitionCN: 生命或成功所必需的。

entries.definition: Demanded by a rule or by the situation.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或情形所要求的。

entries.definition: Too important to be done without.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到不可缺少的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin refusal to yield, put to work in shopping lists, rules and consequences; the family keeps that double life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是拉丁语里「不肯退让」的劲头，后来被用在清单、规则和结果上，同族词一直保留这双重身份。

normal.en: Necesse carries the sense of what will not give way, which is why necessary can mean both required and certain.
normal.cn: necesse 带着「不肯让步」的意味，所以 necessary 既能指「必需」，也能指「必然」。

normal.en: The plural noun necessaries is old-fashioned but correct for a set of daily needs.
normal.cn: 复数名词 necessaries 虽显旧，但指一整套日常所需时是正确的。

normal.en: Unnecessary adds un-, and the word simply reverses: not needed rather than needed.
normal.cn: unnecessary 加了 un-，词义直接反转：不是必需，而是不必要。

normal.en: Necessity names the state, necessitate the act, and necessary the quality, all from one Latin base.
normal.cn: necessity 指状态，necessitate 指动作，necessary 指性质，三者同出一个拉丁词干。

normal.en: If necessary is a fixed phrase that shortens a whole conditional clause into two words.
normal.cn: if necessary 是固定说法，把一个完整条件句压缩成两个词。

abstract.en: A key that opens one door is necessary only because of that door; the word always implies a purpose behind the need.
abstract.cn: 一把钥匙之所以必需，是因为有那扇门；这个词背后总藏着一个目的。

abstract.en: A necessary result is a consequence with no side road, which is why the same adjective can sound like fate.
abstract.cn: 必然结果是一条没有岔路的结果，所以同一个形容词有时听起来像命运。

abstract.en: Calling things necessaries reduces a whole life to a short list of objects that must be carried.
abstract.cn: 把东西叫作 necessaries，等于把一整段生活压缩成一张必须携带的短清单。

examples.en: The repair is necessary before the bridge can reopen.
examples.cn: 桥要重新开放，先得完成这项维修。

examples.en: Sleep is necessary for the body to recover.
examples.cn: 睡眠对身体恢复是必要的。

examples.en: The shelter kept only the bare necessaries for the night.
examples.cn: 收容所只留了过夜最基本的必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢色塞瑞」——必需品总在「呢色」堆里被翻出来；记住 necessary 是必要的、必然的。

root: 拉丁语 necesse（不可避免）一般认为由 ne-（不）与 cedere（退让）构成，派生形容词 necessarius；经古法语 necessaire 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what cannot be done without; the senses then split into practical need, forced consequence, and the plural noun for the objects themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「缺了就不行」；义项分出实际需要、被迫产生的结果，以及直接指物件本身的复数名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turning in a lock that will not open without it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把钥匙插进锁孔，没有它就打不开那扇门。

branches.cn: 清单上有一项被圈了两遍

branches.en: a thermometer rising because the reaction has started
branches.cn: 反应开始后温度计一路上升

branches.en: a suitcase holding only soap, thread and a candle
branches.cn: 行李箱里只有肥皂、线团和一支蜡烛

branches.en: a bridge waiting for one last repair before traffic
branches.cn: 桥等着最后一项维修才放行

branches.en: a shop shelf marked for daily needs
branches.cn: 货架上标着日常所需的那一排

intro.en: A Latin negative, a verb of yielding, an adjective and two English endings build this entry from the inside out.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁否定成分、一个表示退让的动词、一个形容词和两个英语词尾，从内到外搭起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is well recorded: necesse, its derived adjective necessarius, and the verb cedere that the negative element is thought to contain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基有明确记载：necesse、由它派生的形容词 necessarius，以及一般认为藏在否定成分里的动词 cedere。

definition_zh: 必要性；必需品；贫困；必然性；迫不得已
definition_en: the state of being necessary; something that cannot be done without; also poverty or unavoidable need
core_image: 一只空水壶立在桌上，旁边是一张写满“必须”的清单，第一行写着水，后面才是别的。
scene: 救援队在出发前清点物资，队长说，干净的水要排在最前面。Clean water is the first necessity for the team.
sceneCN: 这里 necessity 是“不可或缺的东西、必需品”（第 2 个义项）；句意：干净的水是队伍最首要的必需品；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 必要性；必需品；贫困；必然性；（不得已的）需要

derivatives.zh: 必要的；必然的
必然地；必定
使成为必要；需要

senses.title: The state of being needed
senses.definition: the condition of being required or indispensable for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为达成某目的而被需要、不可缺的状态
senses.example: The report argues the necessity of a second runway at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 报告论证了机场修建第二条跑道的必要性。
senses.why: This is the abstract quality, not the object: it answers the question 'why must this be done?' rather than 'what do we need?'
senses.whyCN: 这是抽象的性质，而不是具体的东西：它回答“为什么非做不可”，而不是“我们需要什么”。

senses.title: Something you cannot do without
senses.titleCN: 必需品：清单上排第一的东西
senses.definition: an item that is essential for living or for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 维持生活或完成某项活动所必需的东西
senses.example: The clinic lacks the basic necessities: clean water, gloves, and bandages.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所缺少基本必需品：干净的水、手套和绷带。
senses.why: The abstract quality turns concrete: if something is necessary, then the thing itself can be called a necessity and counted in a list.
senses.whyCN: 抽象性质具体化了：如果某物是必要的，那么该物本身就可以被称为 necessity，并能列进清单里点算。

senses.title: Hardship and poverty
senses.titleCN: 贫困窘迫：被“必需”逼到角落
senses.definition: the condition of extreme need or poverty, especially when money is short
senses.definitionCN: 极度匮乏或贫困的处境，尤指缺钱的状况
senses.example: Many families were driven by necessity to sell their tools.
senses.exampleCN: 许多家庭因贫困所迫卖掉了工具。
senses.why: When needs cannot be met, necessity stops meaning 'requirement' and starts naming the pressure itself, which is close to want and hardship.
senses.whyCN: 当需求无法满足时，necessity 就不再表示“要求”，而开始指那种压力本身，接近匮乏与困苦。

senses.title: Logical inevitability
senses.titleCN: 逻辑必然：前提逼出结论
senses.definition: the quality of following unavoidably from given premises or laws
senses.definitionCN: 由既定前提或规律不可回避地推出的性质
senses.example: The necessity of the conclusion follows from the two premises.
senses.exampleCN: 该结论的必然性由那两个前提推出。
senses.why: In logic the word marks that a step cannot fail: if the premises hold, the conclusion has no alternative.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑中，这个词标出某一步不可能失手：前提成立，结论就别无选择。

senses.title: What cannot be otherwise
senses.titleCN: 不可避免：事情只能这样发生
senses.definition: the character of an event that could not have happened differently
senses.definitionCN: 某事无法以别的方式发生的性质
senses.example: The historian describes the collapse as a necessity rather than an accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学家把那次崩溃描述为必然，而非意外。
senses.why: Here necessity is applied to events, not to logic: the claim is that conditions left no room for another outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里 necessity 用于事件而非逻辑：主张是条件没有给别的结果留余地。

senses.title: The means of living
senses.titleCN: 生计所需：过日子离不开的
senses.definition: the conditions or resources required to maintain life
senses.definitionCN: 维持生活所必需的条件或资源
senses.example: The workers asked for enough wages to cover the necessities of life.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求足够的工资来支付生活必需品。
senses.why: The plural ties the word to the household: air, water, food, and shelter are necessities because life cannot continue without them.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式把这个词拴在家计上：空气、水、食物和住所之所以是 necessities，是因为缺了它们生活无法继续。

senses.title: Only because one must
senses.titleCN: 迫不得已：不是想，而是不得不
senses.definition: the pressure of circumstances that forces an action one would not otherwise choose
senses.definitionCN: 迫使人们做出本不会选择的行为的处境压力
senses.example: Out of necessity, she took the night shift and gave up her classes.
senses.exampleCN: 迫不得已，她接了夜班，放弃了课程。
senses.why: In the phrase out of necessity, the word names the cause of an unwanted choice: the action is explained, not praised.
senses.whyCN: 在“出于无奈”这一说法里，这个词说明一个并不想要的选择的原因：它是在解释行为，而不是在赞美行为。

senses.title: A category in philosophy
senses.titleCN: 哲学范畴：必然与偶然相对
senses.definition: the philosophical category of what must be, as opposed to what happens by chance
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上“必定如此”的范畴，与偶然相对
senses.example: The dialogue contrasts necessity with chance in the order of the universe.
senses.exampleCN: 这段对话在宇宙秩序中把必然与偶然对照起来。
senses.why: Philosophy turns the everyday pressure into a category: some things are said to be necessary in themselves, not merely needed by someone.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常的压力提升为一个范畴：有些事物被说成自身必然，而不只是被某人需要。

intro.en: Necessity comes from Latin necessitas, from necesse, 'unavoidable'. The internal structure of necesse is disputed, so the word's deeper root is best marked as uncertain.
intro.cn: necessity 来自拉丁语 necessitas，出自 necesse“不可避免”。necesse 的内部结构存在争议，因此更深的词根应标为来源不确定。

items.en: Necesse meant unavoidable or indispensable. It was already used both for logical compulsion and for the pressure of circumstances.
items.cn: necesse 意为“不可避免的、不可或缺的”，当时既用于逻辑强制，也用于处境的压力。

items.en: The noun added the senses of compulsion, need, poverty, and bonds of duty. It could name both an inner must and an outer shortage.
items.cn: 名词形式增加了强制、需要、贫困与义务约束等义，既能指内在的“必须”，也能指外在的匮乏。

items.en: The commonly repeated split ne- 'not' plus cedere 'yield' would mean 'not yielding'. This is a plausible reconstruction, not a confirmed derivation, so it is marked uncertain.
items.cn: 常见的拆解是 ne-“不”加 cedere“让步”，意为“不让步”。这是一种合理的重构，并非已确认的派生，故标为来源不确定。

items.en: Old French necessité carried the senses of need, compulsion, and want. English borrowed the word in the 14th century through French.
items.cn: 古法语 necessité 带有需要、强制与匮乏等义。英语于 14 世纪经法语借入该词。

items.en: English necessity first covered compulsion and need, then widened to include indispensable objects and the philosophical category of inevitability.
items.cn: 英语 necessity 最初涵盖强制与需要，随后扩展到不可或缺的物品，以及哲学上的必然性范畴。

items.en: The plural necessities settled into household and economic language, giving phrases such as daily necessities and bare necessities.
items.cn: 复数 necessities 固定于家庭与经济语境，形成 daily necessities、bare necessities 等说法。

note.en: The first group is the necessary word family; the second compares words for needs and for inevitability.
note.cn: 第一组是 necessary 的词族；第二组比较表示“需要”与“必然”的词。

entries.definition: required, or certain to happen. It describes a thing or a conclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 必需的，或必定发生的；描述事物或结论。

entries.definition: to make something necessary. It names the cause, not the need.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要；命名的是原因，不是需要本身。

entries.definition: in every case, or as a logical consequence. It often appears in negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 在所有情况下，或作为逻辑结果；常出现在否定句中。

entries.definition: absolutely important or basic. It grades importance but does not claim that something cannot be omitted.
entries.definitionCN: 绝对重要或基本的；它给重要性分级，但不宣称不可省略。

entries.definition: something officially demanded or needed for a purpose. It comes from a rule or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的被正式要求或需要之物；来源于规定或权威。

entries.definition: the quality of being impossible to avoid. It stresses the future, while necessity can be logical.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免的性质；侧重未来，而 necessity 可以是逻辑上的。

entries.definition: the state of lacking money or goods. It is one concrete sense of necessity, not the whole word.
entries.definitionCN: 缺钱或缺物的状态；它只是 necessity 的一个具体义项。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin necesse, unavoidable, plus the noun suffix -itas, which became English -ity. The word names the 'must' itself.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 necesse“不可避免”，加名词后缀 -itas（英语作 -ity）。这个词命名的是“必须”本身。

normal.en: A necessity is whatever stands first on the list when everything else is crossed out.
normal.cn: necessity 就是把其他都划掉后仍留在清单第一行的东西。

normal.en: Out of necessity means the choice was made by circumstances, not by preference.
normal.cn: out of necessity 意味着选择是处境做的，不是偏好做的。

normal.en: Water, food, shelter: plural necessities are the household version of the abstract word.
normal.cn: 水、食物、住所：复数的 necessities 就是这个词的家计版本。

normal.en: In a proof, necessity is the step that cannot be skipped.
normal.cn: 在证明里，necessity 就是那步不能跳过的地方。

normal.en: Necessity and necessary share one spine; only the ending changes the job.
normal.cn: necessity 与 necessary 共享同一根脊梁，只是词尾改变了词性。

abstract.en: Necessity is a mirror held up to desire: it shows how much of what we call 'must' is only 'would like'.
abstract.cn: necessity 是一面照向欲望的镜子：它照出我们称为“必须”的东西里，有多少其实只是“想要”。

abstract.en: Every claim of necessity removes an option, and whoever defines necessity controls the choices of others.
abstract.cn: 每一次“必然”的宣称都在删掉一个选项；谁定义必然，谁就掌握了他人的选择。

abstract.en: The word ties a physical shortage to a logical conclusion, as if what is missing could prove what must be.
abstract.cn: 这个词把物质匮乏与逻辑结论绑在一起，仿佛缺什么就能证明什么必然如此。

examples.en: The engineers questioned the necessity of the extra tower, given the new safety system.
examples.cn: 鉴于新的安全系统，工程师们质疑了额外那座塔的必要性。

examples.en: In the drought year, water became a necessity that the town rationed by the bucket.
examples.cn: 干旱那年，水成了小镇按桶配给的必需品。

examples.en: Of necessity, the team shipped the simple version first and saved the refinements for later.
examples.cn: 不得已之下，团队先交付了简单版本，把改进留到以后。

dict_mnemonic.text: ne（不）+ cess（退）+ ity——一步也不退，就是“必要、必然”；不退的东西就是必需品。

root: 源自拉丁语 necessitas（必然、需要、困乏），出自 necesse（不可避免的）；其更早的词根拆解存在争议，通常的说法是 ne-“不”加 cedere“让步”，但未获确证，应视为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of necessity, from abstract requirement to concrete goods, hardship, and logical compulsion. The shared core is a door that will not open: something that cannot be refused, omitted, or otherwise arranged.
sensesIntro.cn: necessity 的八个义项，从抽象要求到具体物品、贫困与逻辑强制。共同的核心是一扇打不开的门：某个东西无法被拒绝、省略或另行安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty water jug beside a list whose first line reads water, with everything else below it.
core.cn: 核心意象：空水壶旁一张清单，第一行写着水，其余都排在下面。

branches.en: COMPULSION: a required condition and a forced conclusion both leave no alternative.
branches.cn: 强制：必需的条件与被迫的结论，都不留别的可能。

branches.en: THE THING NEEDED: from a clinic's clean water to a household's means of living.
branches.cn: 被需要之物：从诊所的干净水到家庭的生计来源。

branches.en: PRESSURE: poverty and 'out of necessity' both describe circumstances forcing a choice.
branches.cn: 压力：贫困与“迫不得已”都描述处境逼迫下的选择。

branches.en: EVENTS THAT COULD NOT DIFFER: history read as inevitability rather than accident.
branches.cn: 无法两样的事件：把历史读成必然而非偶然。

branches.en: A PHILOSOPHICAL CATEGORY: necessity set against chance in the order of things.
branches.cn: 哲学范畴：在万物秩序中把必然与偶然对置。

intro.en: Necessity is Latin necesse plus -ity, the noun suffix from -itas. The family runs through necessary, necessitate, and necessarily, with un- forming the negative.
intro.cn: necessity 是拉丁语 necesse 加 -ity（源自 -itas 的名词后缀）。词族包括 necessary、necessitate、necessarily，并用 un- 构成否定。

latinIntro.en: The base is necesse, unavoidable, with the noun necessitas and the adjective necessarius. The deeper root of necesse is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 necesse“不可避免”，名词 necessitas，形容词 necessarius。necesse 的更早词根存在争议。

items.example: A visa is necessary for entry into the country.

items.meaning: the state of being needed, or the thing needed
items.example: The war turned bread into a daily necessity.
items.exampleCN: 战争让面包成了日常必需品。

items.meaning: in every case, or by logical consequence
items.example: A higher price does not necessarily mean better quality.
items.exampleCN: 价格更高并不必然意味着质量更好。

items.example: The repair will necessitate closing the road for a week.
items.exampleCN: 这项维修将使道路必须关闭一周。

items.example: The extra form added an unnecessary delay.
items.exampleCN: 那张额外的表格造成了不必要的延误。

items.meaning: things needed for a purpose, especially in law and trade
items.meaningCN: 所需物品，尤用于法律与贸易语境
items.example: The contract covered the necessaries for the voyage.
items.exampleCN: 合同涵盖了此次航行所需的物品。

items.meaning: poor or needy; in urgent want
items.example: The fund was set up for necessitous families.
items.exampleCN: 这项基金是为贫困家庭设立的。

items.meaning: the goods needed for daily life
items.example: The shelter stores blankets and other necessities.
items.exampleCN: 收容所存放毯子和其他生活必需品。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可避免的；不可或缺的

definition_zh: 颈；脖子；领口；（瓶、琴等的）细长颈部；地峡；拥吻
definition_en: the part of the body joining the head to the shoulders; a narrow joining part of an object; the opening of a garment; a narrow strip of land; and, informally, to kiss and hold someone closely
core_image: 一双手环绕在头与肩之间，把两端连成一条柔软的通道

pos.zh: 颈；脖子；领口；细长颈部；地峡

senses.title: The part joining the head to the body
senses.definition: the narrow part of the body that connects the head to the shoulders and chest
senses.definitionCN: 连接头部与肩胸之间那段较窄的身体部位
senses.example: The cat rubbed its neck against the door frame.
senses.exampleCN: 猫把脖子蹭在门框上。
senses.why: Old English hnecca named the narrow bridge between head and trunk; the shape of a constriction between two wider ends is what the word first points at.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hnecca 指的就是头与躯干之间那条窄窄的桥；这个词最早指向的是「两端宽、中间收窄」的形状。

senses.title: A narrow joining part of an object
senses.definition: the long narrow part of an object, such as a bottle or a stringed instrument, that joins it to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 瓶子、弦乐器等物件上细长的连接部分
senses.example: The label was glued around the neck of the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 标签被粘在瓶颈上。
senses.why: Any object shaped like that bridge lends its narrow joining part the same name, because the picture is a constriction between two wider ends.
senses.whyCN: 任何物件只要长得像那条桥，它的细长连接处就借用了同一个名字，因为画面仍是「两端宽、中间收」。

senses.title: The opening of a garment
senses.definition: the part of a shirt, dress or sweater that surrounds the neck and is shaped to fit it
senses.definitionCN: 衬衫、连衣裙或毛衣上围着脖子、按颈部形状裁出的开口
senses.example: She pulled the sweater down over a wide neck.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毛衣往下拉，盖住宽大的领口。
senses.why: The garment opening sits exactly where the body's neck passes through, so the word transfers from the body to the cloth that surrounds it.
senses.whyCN: 衣服的开口正好位于脖子穿过的地方，于是这个词从身体转到了包住身体的那层布上。

senses.title: A narrow strip of land between waters
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas of land and has water on either side
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大陆地、两侧临水的狭长地带
senses.example: The village stood on a low neck of land between two bays.
senses.exampleCN: 村子坐落在两个海湾之间一块低矮的地峡上。
senses.why: A strip of land with water on both sides looks like a narrow joining piece, so the same word is used for an isthmus.
senses.whyCN: 两侧临水的一条陆地，看起来就像一块窄窄的连接件，所以同一个词也被用来指地峡。

senses.title: To kiss and hold someone closely, in informal use
senses.definition: in informal speech, to kiss and caress someone while holding them close
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示搂着某人亲吻、抚摸
senses.example: Two teenagers were necking on a bench by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 两个少年在湖边的长椅上拥吻。
senses.why: Two people holding each other head to head put their necks close together, and English took the body part as a verb for that embrace.
senses.whyCN: 两个人耳鬓相贴地抱在一起时，脖子挨得最近；英语便拿这个身体部位作动词，指这种拥抱。

intro.en: Neck is a Germanic body word whose deeper origin is uncertain, and it has spread from the body to bottles, clothes and land.
intro.cn: neck 是日耳曼语的身体词，更早的来源不确定；它从身体扩展到瓶子、衣服和土地。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some accounts link the Germanic word to a root for bending or pressing together, but this is not settled.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定；有说法把它与表示「弯曲、压紧」的词根联系起来，但并未定论。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as hnakkaz is generally given for the Germanic word for the back of the neck.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语中表示颈背的词有一个类似 hnakkaz 的重构形式。

items.en: Old English hnecca named the neck or nape, and the initial hn- was still pronounced at that stage.
items.cn: 古英语 hnecca 指颈或颈背，当时词首的 hn- 还要发音。

items.en: Middle English dropped the initial h and wrote nekke, the shape that leads towards the modern spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉了词首的 h，写作 nekke，这个形状一路通向现代拼写。

items.en: Modern English keeps neck for the body part and extends it to narrow parts of objects, the opening of clothes, a strip of land and an informal verb.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 neck 指身体部位，并扩展到物件细长处、衣服开口、狭长陆地，还多了一个口语动词。

note.cn: 形近组收仍保留这个词的复合词；近义组收相邻的身体部位与衣着用语。

normalIntro.en: One Old English body word, a lost h, and a habit of naming any narrow join after it: that is the whole history in brief.
normalIntro.cn: 一个古英语身体词、一个消失的 h，以及见到窄连接处就借用的习惯，就是这段历史的大概。

normal.en: Old English hnecca began with hn-, and Middle English simply dropped the h to give nekke.
normal.cn: 古英语 hnecca 以 hn- 开头，中古英语直接把 h 去掉，成了 nekke。

normal.en: Neckline and necklace are compounds that keep the body sense: the line and the jewellery both sit at the neck.
normal.cn: neckline 与 necklace 都是保留身体义的复合词：领口线和首饰都落在脖子处。

normal.en: A bottleneck borrows the shape, not the body: a bottle's narrow part holds traffic or work back.
normal.cn: bottleneck 借的是形状而不是身体：瓶子的细处把交通或工作卡住。

normal.en: Neck and neck pictures two horses whose heads are level, hence the meaning 'exactly equal'.
normal.cn: neck and neck 想像两匹马齐头并进，于是有了「不相上下」的意思。

normal.en: Break one's neck is violent in form but often means rushing dangerously fast.
normal.cn: break one's neck 字面很凶，实际常指拼命赶路、快得危险。

abstract.en: The neck is where a large head is balanced on a narrow support, which is why the word suits any risky narrow join.
abstract.cn: 脖子是让大脑袋架在窄支柱上的地方，所以这个词也适合任何危险的窄连接处。

abstract.en: A garment opening and a body part share one name because cloth is cut to follow the body it covers.
abstract.cn: 衣服开口与身体部位共用一个名字，因为布料是照着它所覆盖的身体裁出来的。

abstract.en: A neck of land is a place where two large worlds touch through a thin corridor.
abstract.cn: 地峡是两片大世界通过一条细走廊相接的地方。

definition_en: a thin pointed tool used for sewing; a hollow needle used to give medicine; the pointer of an instrument; a thin leaf of a pine; and, as a verb, to provoke or tease someone
core_image: 一根细亮的钢针穿过布面，针眼里拖着一根线
scene: 台灯下，奶奶把线头在嘴边抿湿，一次次往针眼里送，终于穿了过去。She threaded the needle on the third try and began mending the torn sleeve.
